rationale: The gated geometry is internally consistent and the liability-side profit-coverage leg is a genuine addition beyond RMW, but oibdp/(dltt+dlc+xint) has an unstable near-zero denominator for low-leverage firms that will likely dominate the z-score and needs explicit winsorization or a leverage floor, and the underlying idea sits close to the published distress/value-trap literature.

(oancf − ib)/at is the negative of total accruals, so the signal is the Sloan (1996) accruals anomaly restricted to high book-to-market firms — a well-documented interaction (accruals are strongest in value/low-quality segments) rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.

A one-year change in ROA applied inside a high book-to-market gate is essentially the ΔROA component of Piotroski's (2000) F-score strategy, which was published precisely as fundamental-signal screening within value stocks, so this is a rediscovery rather than a repair.

The expression, gate direction, and positive expected sign are mutually consistent and the glamour-side mirror is a legitimate diagnostic that isolates where the value–profitability interaction is generated, though it is a symmetric variant of a Piotroski-style ΔROA screen and its incremental content over the cheap-side version may be thin.

Holding profitability high and letting log book-to-market generate the spread reduces the signal to the classic value effect on a profitable subsample — the proposal itself concedes it retains HML exposure, so it is near-guaranteed to be absorbed by FF5 and is too trivial a construction to be worth a slot.

This combines two well-published anomalies — intangible/R&D-adjusted book-to-market (Park; Eisfeldt-Kim-Papanikolaou) and gross profitability (Novy-Marx) — and the claim that the restated valuation leg cannot be absorbed by HML is unsupported since cumulative-R&D-adjusted B/M is very highly correlated with raw B/M for the large majority of firms where COALESCE sets R&D to zero.
